title: Piaget used a shaken rattle as an example of learning what an action does
summary: OpenStax says Piaget thought that learning a rattle makes a noise when shaken grew slowly as a child acted on things.
body: OpenStax Psychology says Piaget thought children's ability to understand objects, such as learning that a rattle makes a noise when shaken, developed slowly as a child matured and interacted with the environment. The rattle is his example of an action with a heard result. The sentence is the textbook's picture of his view. It is not a count of how many babies shake rattles.

sources.title: OpenStax Psychology, 9.3 Stages of Development
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Psychology web page, CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase; credit OpenStax. Supports the rattle-when-shaken example in the paragraph on Piaget and object understanding.
